neighbours.label: a function word (to, a, for) inside a fixed adverbial idiom such as 'to a large extent', 'for instance', 'a city to see'
fire: Rainfall is, to a great degree, controlled by the mountains.
Some fruits, for example, ripen after they are picked.
His success was to some extent a matter of luck.
Kyoto is a place to experience old Japan at its best.
Older cars, for instance, lack modern airbags.
The plan worked to a certain extent, but costs rose.
Two novels and a play are to her credit so far.
The outcome was in large part a result of the weather.
quiet: Rainfall moved from the coast to the mountains overnight.
Some fruits were picked for the market this morning.
His brother drove to the station in the rain.
Kyoto is a city with many temples and old streets.
Older cars were sold for parts at the auction.
The plan was sent to the board for approval.
Two novels and a play were sent to her editor.
The outcome was announced on the radio at noon.

short: function word in a fixed idiom
notes: probe: 'to a large extent' 0.78, 'a city to see' 0.61, 'for instance' 0.40. Near misses keep to/for in literal uses.
